Core Case Linking / Relationship Management
2.2.16
The system must allow users to link cases regardless of case type, including linking to cases that do not exist within the CMS using a designated reference number field.
2.2.17
The system must allow authorized users to remove case links.
2.2.34
The system must retain linkage history when cases are de-linked, consolidated, or separated, including effective dates and reasons.
Related Case Creation / Association
1.4.8
The system must support initiating related-but-separate cases (e.g., co-defendant/co-minor/co-sibling scenarios) that share selected data elements while remaining distinct cases with independent lifecycle processing.
1.2.11
The system must support grouping related records under a single case with subordinate identifiers while maintaining linkage and traceability.
Cross-Case Data / Behavior
2.1.24
The system must automatically populate a non-criminal case with information from a linked criminal case based on predetermined criteria.
2.1.31
The system must identify and flag conflicting data values across linked cases and provide tools to reconcile discrepancies.
2.05.40
The system must evaluate dependencies across linked or related cases and warn users when an action on one case may impact another.
Coordination vs Consolidation (Important Distinction)
2.2.41
The system must support “coordination” of cases (heard together without transfer of data) distinct from consolidation.
2.2.22
The system must support consolidation of multiple cases into a single case record while maintaining traceability.
2.2.43
The system must support de-consolidation of previously consolidated cases with controlled record movement.
Multi-Case Structures / References
2.2.42
The system must support association of multiple case numbers and formats to a proceeding and support filing under a controlling case number.
Cross-Case Document & Data Behavior
2.3.20
The system must support pre-populating merged documents using information from any linked case.
Notifications / Scheduling Awareness
2.06.12
The system must notify users of co-defendant or related cases during scheduling.
Reporting / Visibility
2.12.06
The system must allow authorized users to view all cases related to an individual, including linked cases, subject to security rules.
Post-Disposition / Non-Case Linking
5.2.67
The system must merge non-case records into a future initiated case while maintaining traceability.
5.2.71
The system must link non-case records to related parties, cases, or events while preserving traceability.
Appeals Linking (Trial ↔ Appellate)
6.2.73
The system must record filing of appeals and associate each appeal with the originating case.
6.2.77
The system must preserve linkage between originating case and all appellate cases, including successive appeals.

For example, a user could open a pleading, order, exhibit, or filing from:

Case summary
Filings/document list
Event or hearing screen
Hearing activity record
Party or docket view, if applicable

The purpose is usability: wherever the user is working, the related document should be accessible in context.

G.value: The system must support suspension, modification, and override of time-standard counting under configured conditions, with required reason and audit tracking.

H.value:
Time-counting suspension and override governance

It means the system should be able to adjust how case time standards are calculated when certain circumstances apply.

For example, the system may normally count how many days a case has been pending or whether a hearing/disposition deadline is approaching. But in some situations, the clock may need to pause, change, or be overridden, such as when:

A case is stayed
A defendant fails to appear
A party is unavailable
A required evaluation is pending
A continuance changes the applicable timeline
A case enters diversion or another alternate workflow
A judge or authorized user approves an exception

The “required reason and audit tracking” part means the system should require the user to document why the time standard was changed and preserve who made the change, when, and what changed.
